title: Questions to ask, and the diagnosis talk-track
objectives: Ask the four diagnosis questions in order.
Use the talk-track to agree what will be checked before any decision.
body_md:
Questions to ask: “When will you need this money?” “What return were you expecting, and over what period?” “Have you added or stopped anything since you started?” “How does the fund compare with its benchmark over the same dates?”

> **Talk-track:** “Let's check four things before deciding anything: the right return measure, the time it's had, the benchmark, and your goal date. Then we'll know whether there's really a problem.”

> **Investor takeaway:** Before blaming the timing, check the measure, the horizon, the expectation and the fund.
example: Client: “My fund isn't growing.” Ask: when do you need it, what return did you expect over what period, what changed since you started, and how does it compare with its benchmark?
say: Check four things before deciding anything.
Decide by the goal date, not by the headline.
never: Compare the fund with last year's top fund.

talk_track.title: Four checks first
talk_track.text: Let's check four things before deciding anything: the right return measure, the time it's had, the benchmark, and your goal date. Then we'll know whether there's really a problem.

check.q: Which question comes first in the diagnosis?
check.why: Questions to ask: “When will you need this money?” first.

check.q: Why compare the fund with its benchmark over the same dates?
o: To tell a market-wide fall from a fund problem
check.why: Market phase: did the whole market or category fall? Fund and benchmark both down means normal volatility.

check.q: A client expected last year's 40% to repeat. Which cause is that?
check.why: Wrong expectation: what return did the client expect, and why? Expected last year's 40% to repeat.
